title: Convexity of the corrected Gaussian profile sum
statement: Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $a-b>0$ and $a+b<1$. The function $x\mapsto U(a+x)^2+U(a-x)^2+2(1-Q(a)^2)x^2$ is convex on the interval $[-b,b]$, where $Q$ is the total Gaussian quantile and $U(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ is the total Gaussian isoperimetric profile.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. If $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $a-b>0$ and $a+b<1$, then $x\mapsto I(a+x)^2+I(a-x)^2+2(1-Q(a)^2)x^2$ is convex on $[-b,b]$. Here $Q(p)=0$ and $I(p)=\varphi(0)$ outside $(0,1)$, and $[-b,b]$ may be empty.
